title: Chapter 90 — Running Yourself by Numbers: The Measurement Mindset
intro: The measurement mindset, leading vs. lagging indicators, and the discipline of honest data.

sections.title: Compete Against Your Best
sections.content:
Do not compete against the industry average. Compete against your own best performance.

Industry averages describe what is common. They do not describe what is possible. The salesperson who says 'I am closing at 25% which is the industry average' has made average their ceiling.

The salesperson who says 'I closed at 32% last quarter — how do I get to 38%?' is on a completely different trajectory. Same floor. Same products. Different mindset.

sections.title: Leading vs. Lagging Indicators
sections.content:
Your closing percentage is a lagging indicator. It tells you what already happened. You cannot change it after the fact.

Leading indicators tell you what is about to happen. Number of customers engaged today. Number of demos completed. Number of follow-ups made. Number of CRM entries updated.

If you focus on improving leading indicators, the lagging indicators follow. If you focus only on lagging indicators, you are staring at a scoreboard without playing the game.

sections.title: Honest Data
sections.content:
The most important thing about your personal metrics is that they are honest. If you underreport ups to inflate your closing percentage, you are lying to yourself. That does not make you look better. It makes it impossible to diagnose problems.

Track everything accurately. The truth is the only thing that helps you improve.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating measurement mindset, ask:

Does the salesperson track their own numbers — or only look when management asks?
Do they focus on leading indicators they can control — or only lagging indicators they cannot?
Is their data honest — or gamed?
Are they competing against their own best — or just matching the average?
